clue.text: Calm river in Ireland, for example

parts.note: to compose yourself is to calm down
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A tranquil river somewhere in the Irish countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ireland' looks like the country, but it is John Ireland, the English composer of songs and piano music.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ireland was an English twentieth-century writer of music, so he is one example of the category.

clue.text: New constellation initially noticed in the West

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are formed into a fresh arrangement
initially points to the very start of the word before it, keeping only its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of constellation
taken as written, to be shuffled with the C

explanation.surface: An astronomer spots a new group of stars appearing in the western sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New constellation' reads as one phrase, but New is the anagram signal and only the first letter of constellation joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Occident is a formal name for the western world, as opposed to the Orient in the east.

clue.text: Like Lincoln, say, quiet and suitable to live in

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
a residential area is one meant for homes

explanation.surface: A description of Abraham Lincoln as a calm man in a pleasant, homely place.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln held the office of US president, so anything relating to that office or its holders fits.

clue.text: Succession of queen's arranged with church

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters before it are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The line of royal succession sorted out with the Church's blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests royal succession, but the definition is just the general word for a series in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A succession is a series of things following one after another in order, which is what a sequence is.

clue.text: Desperate struggle for artist to make drawing

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the stock crossword artist
a trace is a drawing copied through thin paper

explanation.surface: A painter struggles desperately to produce a sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the fierce, exhausting competition of modern working life to get ahead.

clue.text: King, in play, has nothing available when bishop and queen move in

indicators.note: moving in means taking up residence inside, so these letters go inside the others

parts.note: O is the figure zero
something on is available, as in on offer
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A chess game where the king has nothing left once bishop and queen advance.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess pieces and 'move' suggest a game of chess, but the play is a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is the king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Decoration for instrument

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a medal or honour
second meaning: a metal disc struck with a beater

explanation.walkthrough: A gong is British slang for a medal or honour, as in an award from the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a medal or official honour, and also a percussion disc hit with a padded hammer.

clue.text: Books put out in litter bin, unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the word lacks its ending, so its final letter goes
put out means disturbed or upset, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
bin without its last letter

explanation.surface: Books thrown out into the rubbish bin, left half-done.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera's printed text is its book, and libretti is the plural of libretto.

clue.text: 1 ac making name in England with one

indicators.note: the name is put to work inside the word for England, making its middle

parts.note: Albion is the poetic old name for Britain or England
N is the abbreviation for name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue: a composer makes his name in England with one piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 ac stands for the answer to 1 across, COMPOSER, which is the definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomaso Albinoni was a Venetian Baroque writer of concertos and operas, so he is one of the 1 across category.

clue.text: Top marks collected by expert

indicators.note: things collected by someone are gathered up and held within

parts.note: an ace is someone highly skilled
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: An expert scores the highest marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top marks' reads as one phrase, but Top alone is the definition and marks are the old Deutschmarks.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point or peak of something, so it means the top.

clue.text: Old-fashioned hardship, say, in sailing vessel

parts.note: square is slang for conventional and out of date

indicators.note: say means as spoken, so the word is pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: rigour means severity or hardship

explanation.surface: Life aboard an old sailing ship was hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A square-rigger is a ship whose main sails are set across the hull on horizontal yards, an old type of sailing ship.

clue.text: Like a great opportunity to overcharge for sought-after coat

parts.note: a golden opportunity is an excellent one
to fleece someone is to cheat them out of money

explanation.surface: A trader sees a great chance to overcharge for a coat everyone wants.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about pricing fashion; the coat is the ram's fleece Jason went looking for.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Jason and the Argonauts quested for the ram's precious hide, the most sought-after coat in legend.

clue.text: Visibly show exertion as run ended in distress

indicators.note: in distress means troubled and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner finishes the race exhausted, plainly suffering from the effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard physical effort makes the face flush, so turning red in the face is a visible sign of strain.

clue.text: Prisoner caught in moving struggle

parts.note: a con is a convict

indicators.note: something caught in another thing is trapped inside it

parts.note: to flit is to move house, often secretly
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A prisoner gets caught up in a fight while being transferred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught in' does double duty: caught supplies the letter C, which then goes inside the word for moving.
explanation.definitionFit: A conflict is a fight or serious disagreement, so it works as a noun for a struggle.

clue.text: Cad joins up again? Just the reverse

indicators.note: the reverse tells us to read the phrase back to front

parts.note: to reknit is to join together again

explanation.surface: A bounder patches things up and returns, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the definition by example is loose: rejoined things are reknitted.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinker is an informal word for a thoroughly unpleasant or contemptible person, just like a cad.

clue.text: Minor event involving teams — in what way?

parts.note: teams are sides in a game
how asks in what manner

explanation.surface: Someone puzzled asks how a small sporting fixture with teams actually works.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideshow is a lesser attraction at a fair, or any minor event that distracts from the main business.

clue.text: Dog in miserable state I found

parts.note: base means low and wretched
NJ is the abbreviation for New Jersey, a US state
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds a stray dog in a wretched condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miserable state' reads as one phrase about the dog's condition, but state is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is a small African hunting breed known for not barking.

clue.text: Publicise the main broadcasting channels

parts.note: to air an idea is to make it public
the main is the open sea, and the waves are a poetic name for it

explanation.surface: An instruction to promote the leading TV channels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' looks like it means the principal channels; it is the old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The airwaves are the radio frequencies used to transmit radio and television signals.

clue.text: Mountain where psychiatrist takes foreign woman

parts.note: Carl Jung was the Swiss founder of analytical psychology
Frau is German for woman or wife
joins the two parts in order

explanation.surface: A Swiss mountain where a famous psychiatrist brings a woman from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jungfrau is a high Alpine peak in the Bernese Oberland of Switzerland.

clue.text: Dog or cat to mollycoddle

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails was a whip used for flogging
to pet is to pamper or fuss over

explanation.surface: Choosing between a dog or a cat to pamper as a household pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog or cat' looks like a choice of pet; or is only a link, and cat is the old naval whip.
explanation.definitionFit: The whippet is a slim, fast breed of racing dog related to the greyhound.

clue.text: Garment a good-looking girl's taken in to make smaller

indicators.note: something taken in is received inside, so these letters are swallowed by the others

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: A pretty girl's dress is altered by a seamstress to fit a smaller size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests dressmaking alteration; here it means the garment goes inside the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish something is to reduce it in size or amount, the same as making it less.

clue.text: Sort of coal first put out fire

indicators.note: first put out means the opening letter is removed from the word

parts.note: lignite is soft brown coal

explanation.surface: Someone extinguishes a coal fire before it gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out fire' reads as extinguishing, the opposite of the answer; fire is a verb meaning set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire something can mean to set it burning, so the verb means to set alight.

clue.text: Financial return brings cheer when in debt

indicators.note: when it is in something, it is placed inside it

parts.note: in the red means overdrawn, in debt
fun is merriment

explanation.surface: Getting your money back is welcome news when you are overdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Bank statements printed debts in red, hence red for debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A refund is money paid back to a customer, so it is a financial return.

clue.text: Disposing of silver, in the event, of course

definitions.meaning: first meaning: getting rid of the family silverware for cash
second meaning: a type of race run on a racecourse

explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as naturally; it means on a racecourse. A selling plate is a minor horse race whose winner must be put up for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means flogging silverware, and is also a low-grade horse race after which the winner is auctioned.

clue.text: Stuff found in drink, in ale especially

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: letters two to five of the phrase

explanation.surface: Sediment turns up in a drink, especially in beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lees are the dregs or sediment that settle at the bottom of wine or beer.

clue.text: Make new organ, initially

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the word it follows, keeping just its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of new

explanation.surface: An instruction to build a new organ, perhaps a church organ.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money is to gain it by working, so the verb fits as a sense of make.

clue.text: Dish cooked in 'ouse by tenant, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the apostrophe drops the H, as a Cockney would: home becomes 'ome
a lettee is the person to whom property is let

explanation.surface: A tenant cooks a meal at home, in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'ouse tells you to drop the H from home as well.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is a dish of beaten eggs fried in a pan, so it is a cooked dish.

clue.text: Possibly test a sprout? This'll help check the flavour

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of the letters

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a bud is a young shoot

explanation.surface: A cook samples a Brussels sprout to judge its flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste buds are the sensory organs on the tongue that detect sweet, salt, sour and bitter.
